title: Record that low_weight_words matches the reflected P112 transported supports
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Set comparison of one published iterator. No new κ. The selected conditional exponent stays `781451/250000000`.

On the reflected 36-generator basis recorded by open PR #7017, `low_weight_words` from `research/e7-bitsliced-exhaustion/binary.py`, at its default batch size 16 and weight bound 16, returns zero and the seven transported weight-16 supports. The SHA256 of `json.dumps` of those seven sorted integers is `9ce7e5edc72ee3104d62cb068146b73840e9a3c42c4132403dece70c8146cccb`.

The call enumerates every coefficient vector of this independent basis once: a Gray walk of length `2^20` over the high generators, and `2^16` lanes for the low generators. The coefficient-partition argument in `research/e7-bitsliced-exhaustion/PROOF.md` supplies the lane arithmetic. This package checks the hypotheses of that argument on this input and compares the yielded set with the transported supports. It does not reprove the lane arithmetic.

This is an exhaustive finite census of the weight-at-most-16 words of this one ordered basis, through this one call. It is not a half-split census, not a statement about another batch size, and not a result about every generator matrix. A failed search was not used. Selected κ is unchanged.

## Task and overlap

Base `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. Task card `replay-runtime`, priority revision 8. Scope status **refined**.

The card asks for a measured speedup that keeps coverage. The revision-8 verification row says faster output is the same coverage only after the sets are compared. Open PR #7017 recorded the reflected half-split and left this iterator question open. This package answers that question at batch size 16.

Ordered overlap check on 2026-11-10, after fetching upstream `main` at that commit. `scripts/find_overlap.py --refresh` read 339 open pull requests (fetched `2026-11-10T10:27:07Z`, pagination complete) and 7013 discussion records (fetched `2026-11-10T10:28:11Z`, pagination complete), with 10178 local notes and a complete inventory. The hash and the reflected iterator question match open PR #7017 and [discussion #1166 comment 19514152](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19514152). Both state the question and do not run `low_weight_words`. Open PR #7007 is the unreflected comparison at batch size 20. Open PR #7034 is the intersection-counter refusal on the unreflected basis. This package does not redo either of those results.

The reflected basis is rebuilt from `research/p112-rank6-frame-coverage/engine.py` and `research/p112-a3-six-flat/geometry.py`. The 112-line list hash is `a2ac7049d9eef1cff8af1eec35b084e6d261efad5311625e5356cceafe260da7`. The 36 generators have hash `f71157e487ad45377cb6a92651d3a8d8b1055b6978f14a44dea511049ca7da8c`. A local comparison against PR #7017 head `11af08b8ff57dc26492501b4efaffdb34d298a00` found the same ordered basis. That comparison is not a registered input.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library, from the repository root.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-reflected-frame-lane --check-only
python3 -I -B research/p112-reflected-frame-lane/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-reflected-frame-lane
```

Both the direct verifier and the registered runner passed on this machine. The direct call took 486.22 seconds and the registered runner took 278.75 seconds. Those are wall-clock observations, not a speedup claim. The registered command's timeout is 600 seconds.

The verifier requires the transported hash, rejects a dropped support, a weight-15 injection, the seven untransported integers, a repeated generator, and a toy bound change. `verify.py basis` rebuilds the basis and does not call the iterator. That mode is not the registered comparison.

Not run: the #7017 half-split, batch size 20, a reversed generator order, the unreflected iterator, `research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py`, any other simple root, Lean, Docker, and `scripts/research_selected_baseline.py` as a scientific replay.

## Credit

The line list is Cinna Davis's model in `research/p112-rank6-frame-coverage`, from the PR1226/PR1323 E8 listing. The simple system is Nick Petalas's, fixed in `research/p112-a3-six-flat/geometry.py`. `low_weight_words` is Ali Romman's. The unreflected supports are open PR #7007. The reflection, transported integers, free coordinates, and basis weights are open PR #7017.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0. No independent human review and no formal-kernel acceptance are claimed.

## Open next questions

Linked from `research/p112-reflected-frame-lane/README.md`.

1. Does `low_weight_words` at batch size 20 on this same ordered basis return the same seven supports? Batch size 20 is the size used on the unreflected basis. First call that batch on the pinned generator tuple and compare it with the transported hash.
2. Does the reversed 36-tuple, at batch size 16, return the same set? The iterator's result is claimed independent of generator order. First reverse the pinned tuple and repeat the batch-16 call.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The 600-second command cap is what selected batch size 16, the function's default. A short synthetic timing suggested batch 20 would land nearer the cap. One suggestion: state, on the engine card, which single batch size a follow-up should use when a 36-dimensional width-112 call already fills most of the cap. Discussion: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
